entries.reason: the model is per thread, as the header says, so it is kept in thread-local storage and a thread that has set none answers the model a thread starts with; nothing in the library reads that key, so the model is stored and read back and does not change how the release's own cblas_* and LAPACK thread
entries.effect: 0 for a model the library has, -1 for one it has not, and the setting is then left as it was; the model is per thread and a thread that has set none is BLAS_THREADING_MULTI_THREADED. It is a value the port stores and reads back: it does not change how BLAS and LAPACK run, and that is a difference from the header, which documents the call as setting the model those libraries use. Measured on the host, where the call is equally without an effect on the library: four threads inside cblas_sgemm and the process has 15 threads with BLAS_THREADING_MULTI_THREADED and 15 with BLAS_THREADING_SINGLE_THREADED. Measured on the release, which has no model to set: no cache below 18.0 exports an entry point that sets a BLAS threading model, and the one the port calls arrived with the API in 18.0
entries.source: the host's own Accelerate, measured for the default a thread starts with, for a set and for a refused value, and measured for the thread count the library uses with each model; the 18.0 cache, which names both functions where no earlier cache the port holds does, and the absence of any such entry point below it; the enumeration and the two prototypes of the host's vecLib/thread_api.h, read from that header and not from the build SDK, which has no such header
